chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Washa, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The pear repairs the stomach and strengthens it; it and the quince are the same. It is more beneficial when the stomach is full than when it is empty (with saliva). And whoever is afflicted by overwhelming stress, let him eat it, meaning while eating food.
ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of eating pears according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the medicinal properties of pears, noting their ability to 'bind' (yadbugh) and strengthen the stomach, a function shared with quinces. He specifies that they are most effective when consumed with food rather than on an empty stomach, serving as a remedy for 'thakha' (a state of heaviness, drowsiness, or mental fog) to restore clarity and digestion. This reflects the Shia tradition of integrating practical health advice with spiritual well-being, emphasizing moderation and timing in dietary habits.
